title: Setup
---

## Before You Start

Applied R introduces programming from the beginning across eight lessons. Each lesson is planned for 100 minutes, including a 10-minute break. You should be comfortable creating folders and locating files, but no previous R experience is required. Prepare the software and data below before the first session.

Install compatible versions of the following on your computer, using your organisation's software arrangements on a managed device:

1. the [R software](https://cran.r-project.org/mirrors.html) itself, and
2. [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).

If you already have R and RStudio working, use the checks below rather than reinstalling them. If installation is unavailable, tell the organiser before the session so that an appropriate shared-screen or supported-environment fallback can be arranged.

## Create a Project and Obtain the Data

1. Create a folder called `applied_R` in a location you can find again.
2. In RStudio, create a project in that existing folder (**File > New Project > Existing Directory**). See the official [Projects guide](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/code/projects.html).
3. Create a `data` folder inside the project.
4. Download [gapminder_data.csv](../episodes/data/gapminder_data.csv) into `data`. This is a CSV file, so it does not need unzipping.
5. Create and save an R script in the project folder. The loops and tidyverse lessons also use data supplied by the `gapminder` package.

## Prepare the Lesson Packages

Lesson 4 uses `gapminder`, `dplyr` and `readr`. Installing `tidyverse` supplies those packages and `tidyr` for lessons 5 and 6.

Run this once in the R console if these packages are not already available:

```r
install.packages(c("gapminder", "tidyverse"))
```

The retained examples in [lesson 5](../episodes/05-the_tidyverse.qmd) and [lesson 6](../episodes/06-exploration_and_visualisation.qmd) also use the following packages. Prepare them before those lessons:

```r
install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "openxlsx", "gridExtra", "ggExtra", "knitr"))
```

Package installation needs network access. If you see an error, retain the message and ask the organiser which environment or installation route to use. Install packages once; load them again when starting a new R session.

## Check Your Setup

With the `applied_R` project open, run:

```r
library(gapminder)
library(tidyverse)

file.exists("data/gapminder_data.csv")
head(gapminder::gapminder)
sessionInfo()
```

The file check should return `TRUE`, and the dataset should print without a package error. If the file is missing, check `getwd()` and the location of the downloaded CSV. Keep `sessionInfo()` with any request for help so that the R and package versions are visible.

The iteration and data-analysis sessions create an `output` folder for derived files. Keep the course input file unchanged and inspect output destinations before rerunning file-writing examples. The complete course contains eight lessons; the former variables page is now lesson 2 on research data.

## Prepare the Shared Project for Lessons 5–8

Download [research-project.zip](files/research-project.zip){download="research-project.zip"}, extract it and open the extracted `research-project` folder as an RStudio project. Keep the structure intact: `analysis.R`, `report.qmd`, `app.R`, `tests.R`, the README and `data/gapminder_data.csv` belong together. The CSV is a copy of the existing public historical teaching data.

Check from that project's R console:

```r
source("analysis.R")
dat <- read_research_data()
nrow(select_observations(dat, c("Ireland", "Brazil"), 2007))
```

The selection should contain two observations. Once Shiny is available, use `source("tests.R")` to check the complete shared project, including reactive inputs. Do not run the app in the same session while those server tests run.

## Digital Notebook and Dashboard Access

For [lesson 7](../episodes/07-digital_research_notebooks.qmd), install the [Quarto CLI](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) if it is unavailable in RStudio. Check `quarto --version` in a terminal, then open `report.qmd` and use Render. The report needs `knitr` and `rmarkdown`; HTML output avoids requiring a PDF/LaTeX installation.

For [lesson 8](../episodes/08-interactive_research_dashboards.qmd), install Shiny if needed:

```r
install.packages("shiny")
```

With the extracted project open, run `shiny::runApp(".")`. Country/year controls, a figure and table should appear in a browser. Keep the R process running and use Stop/Esc to finish. Install software before class; use a partner's screen or instructor demonstration if access fails. No paid hosting account is required for the local exercises.

Use [Shiny's getting-started guide](https://shiny.posit.co/r/getstarted/) for further help. A rendered report and a live Shiny service have different sharing requirements; deployment is outside classroom setup.

## After Setup

Start with [session 1: R Foundations](../episodes/01-Rstudio_intro.qmd). The learner [Additional Material](additional_material.qmd) page provides a Gapminder practice workflow and further references. Use [Digital Skills Clinics](../../../clinics.qmd) for follow-up help with a specific R or data task.
